Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.5: Anterior Cervical Corpectomy > CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF)
CMM-601.6: Repeat Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) at the Same Level
CMM-601.8: ACDF Following Failed Cervical Disc Arthroplasty Surgery

Required findings: Complete corpectomy or partial corpectomy (i.e., removal of at least one-half of the vertebral body [not for resection of osteophytes alone]) is performed.
The procedure is performed for ANY of the following reasons: infection, trauma, tumor, compression at or behind the level of the vertebral body.
Anterior cervical corpectomy must be performed with a cervical fusion due to the iatrogenic instability of the corpectomy procedure.

Criteria have been met in the applicable procedure-specific section (CMM-601.4: Initial Primary ACDF, CMM-601.6: Repeat ACDF at Same Level, CMM-601.7: Adjacent Segment Disease, or CMM-601.8: ACDF Following Failed Cervical Disc Arthroplasty Surgery).
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.5: Anterior Cervical Corpectomy > CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF)

Non-Indications: Anterior cervical corpectomy without a corresponding fusion.
Corpectomy performed solely for resection of osteophytes.
Procedure not performed for infection, trauma, tumor, or compression at or behind the level of the vertebral body.

Procedure not performed when criteria in CMM-601.4: Initial Primary ACDF, CMM-601.6: Repeat ACDF at Same Level, CMM-601.7: Adjacent Segment Disease, or CMM-601.8: ACDF Following Failed Cervical Disc Arthroplasty Surgery have not been met.
Important criteria & exceptions: Requires a cervical fusion due to iatrogenic instability.
Must be performed for infection, trauma, tumor, or compression at or behind the level of the vertebral body.
Documentation required: Operative report from prior cervical surgery (if applicable).
Cervical MRI or CT radiology reports showing neural compression or pathology requiring corpectomy.
Physical therapy and pharmacy records documenting at least 6 weeks of conservative care.
Objective laboratory cotinine test results confirming nicotine cessation (if applicable).
